abstract: We examine the role of employee health for the restructuring of the labor force during private equity buyouts using employee-level data of 56,000 Dutch buyout employees. We find no evidence that buyouts have a negative impact on the health of buyout employees. Employees lose income and employment after buyouts, and these losses are far larger for employees in poorer health. The negative effect of buyouts on employees’ incomes is buffered by social transfers, and this buffer is larger for employees in poorer health, who exit the labor market at a much higher rate. Health characteristics associated with lower wages in the general population are strongly predictive of job loss after buyouts. This paper was accepted by David Sraer, finance. Funding: This work was supported by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) [Projects MA 3317/3-1 and MA 3317/3-2]. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2022.01874 .
abstract_zh: 我们利用56,000名荷兰私募股权收购企业员工的个体层面数据，考察员工健康在私募股权收购期间劳动力重组中的作用。我们发现，没有证据表明收购会对被收购企业员工的健康产生负面影响。员工在收购后失去收入和就业，而健康状况较差的员工所遭受的这些损失要大得多。收购对员工收入的负面影响被社会转移支付所缓冲，且这种缓冲对健康状况较差的员工更大，因为他们退出劳动力市场的比例要高得多。在一般人群中与较低工资相关的健康特征，对被收购后失业具有强烈的预测作用。本文由David Sraer（金融学）接收。资助：本工作得到德国研究基金会（DFG）[项目MA 3317/3-1和MA 3317/3-2]的支持。补充材料：在线附录和数据文件可在https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2022.01874获取。
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
title: Private Equity Buyouts and Employee Health
title_zh: 私募股权收购与员工健康

abstract: This study revisits the CEO pay-for-performance relation using two methodological innovations designed to address well-known measurement challenges. First, we aggregate pay and performance over the CEO’s entire tenure, allowing us to account for ex post settling up in pay. Second, we use realized compensation rather than ex ante estimates to better capture the actual economic rewards that CEOs receive. We find strong evidence of pay for performance in the full sample with a magnitude 2–10 times greater than that reported in previous studies. However, the pay-for-performance relation is asymmetric. CEOs who outperform their peer firms exhibit strong pay-for-performance sensitivity; those who underperform do not. This asymmetry arises because boards offset weak performance with incremental equity grants, undoing the mechanical correlation that results from declining stock prices. Finally, we show that underperforming CEOs are significantly more likely to be dismissed, suggesting that turnover, rather than lower pay, could be a disciplinary mechanism used by boards. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that tenure-aggregated realized pay better reveals how boards structure incentives and accountability over the full horizon of a CEO’s leadership. This paper was accepted by Ranjani Krishnan, accounting. Funding: We gratefully acknowledge financial support from Columbia Business School, Columbia University. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.04322 .
abstract_zh: 本研究通过两项旨在应对已知计量挑战的方法学创新，重新审视了CEO薪酬与绩效之间的关系。首先，我们将薪酬与绩效在CEO整个任期内进行加总，从而能够考虑薪酬的事后结算。其次，我们使用已实现薪酬而非事前估计，以更好地捕捉CEO实际获得的经济回报。我们在全样本中发现了薪酬与绩效之间强有力的证据，其幅度是此前研究报告的2至10倍。然而，薪酬与绩效之间的关系是非对称的。表现优于同行公司的CEO表现出很强的薪酬与绩效敏感性；表现不佳者则不然。这种非对称性之所以产生，是因为董事会通过增量股权授予来抵消疲弱业绩，从而消除了由股价下跌所导致的机械相关性。最后，我们表明，表现不佳的CEO被解雇的可能性显著更高，这表明人员更替而非较低薪酬，可能是董事会采用的一种纪律机制。总体而言，我们的发现表明，按任期加总的已实现薪酬更好地揭示了董事会在CEO领导力的完整期限内如何构建激励与问责。本文由会计学领域的Ranjani Krishnan接收。资助：我们 gratefully acknowledge financial support from Columbia Business School, Columbia University。补充材料：在线附录和数据文件可在https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.04322获取。
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
title: Long-Term Pay for Performance: Cumulative Evidence over CEO Tenure
title_zh: 长期绩效薪酬：CEO任期内的累积证据

abstract: We examine how the information in public signals (e.g., earnings, analysts’ forecasts) affects firms’ voluntary disclosures. We consider levered firms and information structures such that investors update their beliefs about both the mean and variance of the firm’s cash flows. We predict that firms that, conditional on the public signal, have a higher default risk are less likely to disclose. For firms with low ex ante default risk, larger positive surprises following the public signal initially increase the disclosure likelihood because they indicate a higher mean of cash flows. However, too large positive surprises may reduce the disclosure likelihood of these firms, because the larger surprise is also indicative of higher variance and, thus, higher probability of default. Symmetrically, larger negative surprises may increase disclosure for firms with high ex ante default risk, despite the more pessimistic inference about the mean, because the higher variance makes it more likely that these firms avoid default. Extending our analysis to multiple analysts’ forecasts, we predict that not only consensus, but also dispersion affect firms’ disclosure likelihood. Consensus conveys information about the mean and variance of cash flows, whereas dispersion is informative about the precision of analysts’ signals, which in turn affects the information content of forecasts. This paper was accepted by Suraj Srinivasan, accounting. Funding: D. Lee-Lo gratefully acknowledges financial support from the Accounting Research Center at Kellogg.
abstract_zh: 我们考察公共信号（如盈余、分析师预测）中的信息如何影响企业的自愿披露。我们考虑杠杆企业以及这样的信息结构：投资者会同时更新其对企业现金流均值和方差的信念。我们预测，在给定公共信号的条件下，违约风险更高的企业更不可能进行披露。对于事前违约风险较低的企业，公共信号之后更大的正向意外最初会提高披露可能性，因为它们表明现金流的均值更高。然而，过大的正向意外可能会降低这些企业的披露可能性，因为更大的意外也表明方差更高，从而违约概率更高。对称地，对于事前违约风险较高的企业，更大的负向意外可能会提高披露，尽管对均值的推断更为悲观，因为更高的方差使这些企业更有可能避免违约。将我们的分析扩展到多个分析师预测，我们预测不仅共识，而且离散度也会影响企业的披露可能性。共识传递了关于现金流均值和方差的信息，而离散度则提供了关于分析师信号精确度的信息，这反过来又影响预测的信息含量。本文由会计领域的Suraj Srinivasan接受。资助：D. Lee-Lo 衷心感谢凯洛格商学院会计研究中心的财务支持。
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
title: Public Signals, Default Risk, and Voluntary Disclosure
title_zh: 公共信号、违约风险与自愿披露
